items.title: Cisco 10GBASE SFP+ Modules Data Sheet
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: To pick the right 10G SFP+ optic or direct attach cable for a link and to check its reach, connector, and handling notes before install.
key_procedures_inside: optical and electrical specifications by reach
connector types, LC duplex and Twinax
items.notes: SFP-10G-SR reach is 26m on legacy MMF, 300m on OM3, 400m on OM4, at 850nm over a dual LC/PC connector. Same document also covers passive and active Twinax direct attach copper cables and SFP+ active optical cables (AOC), 1 to 10 meters.

items.title: Cisco 25GBASE SFP28 Modules Data Sheet

key_procedures_inside: optical specifications by reach, 70m OM3 and 100m OM4
items.notes: SFP-25G-SR-S is 850nm over a dual LC/PC connector, max 1.2W, and requires RS-FEC (Reed-Solomon forward error correction) enabled on the host port to operate correctly.

items.title: Cisco 100GBASE QSFP-100G Modules Data Sheet

items.notes: QSFP-100G-SR4-S is the parallel fiber variant that plugs into MPO/MTP trunk cabling rather than a duplex LC patch cord.

items.title: MPO/MTP Array Connectors: Description, Polarity, and Testing
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: To recognize an MPO/MTP trunk connector, tell Type A, B, and C polarity apart, and know how a parallel fiber link gets tested.
key_procedures_inside: identifying the MPO/MTP connector and key orientation
Type A, B, and C polarity per TIA-568
mating adapter key-up versus key-down orientation
OTDR and breakout cable test methods
items.notes: Corning, CommScope, and Panduit polarity guides were tried first, direct guesses and their site search pages, but every attempt came back 403, 404, or a JavaScript only search shell with no fetchable static document. The Fiber Optic Association, a nonprofit fiber optics trade and education body, is used instead and explicitly covers TIA-568 Type A/B/C polarity, which is the core concept a tech needs at the rack.

items.vendor: Intel (IPMI consortium: Intel, HP, Dell, NEC)
items.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification, Second Generation, v2.0 (rev 1.1)
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: The reference for what IPMI sensor readings, event log entries, and chassis power-control commands actually mean on any BMC that predates or sits alongside Redfish.
items.notes: This is the long-standing canonical Intel-hosted URL for the v2.0 rev 1.1 spec used industry-wide (Dell, HPE, and Supermicro BMCs all implement it). WebFetch hit its 10MB size cap on the PDF itself. DMTF's own Redfish specification (DSP0266) was tried instead first for this slot, but dmtf.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every URL tried (the standards index page, the document landing page, and the direct PDF), so it was dropped per the fetch-failure rule; this IPMI spec covers the 'generic IPMI or Redfish reference' requirement instead.
